title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Strict Enforcement of Law in Adjudicating Economic Dispute Cases
keywords_en: fraud; acceptance of bribes; offering bribes; People's Court on trial of economic disputes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Strictly Enforcing the Law in the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases

Fa (Yan) Fa [1985] No. 27

All local people's courts at various levels, all military courts, railway transport courts, and all maritime courts:

Over a period of time, when trying economic dispute cases, people's courts have frequently encountered many cases that cannot be enforced or are difficult to enforce after judgment; it has also been discovered that many cases, on the surface, appear to be economic disputes, but are in essence illegal or criminal acts, even serious crimes, especially the rampant criminal activities of speculation and fraud through the use of economic contracts. This is highly detrimental to the further implementation of the policy of opening up to the outside world and invigorating the domestic economy, to the reform of the socialist economic system, and to the construction of socialist material civilization and spiritual civilization. Therefore, people's courts at all levels must carefully study, correctly judge, and promptly take strict and decisive measures in accordance with the law with respect to the above various situations. Otherwise, it will be impossible to safeguard the interests of the state and the collective, protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, or ensure the smooth progress of the reform of the socialist economic system and the Four Modernizations. To this end, the following notice is hereby given:

1. Where, during the trial of an economic dispute case, a people's court discovers that a judgment may not be enforceable or may be difficult to enforce due to the conduct of one of the parties or for any other reason, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 92 and 93 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), render a ruling on litigation preservation measures such as sealing up, seizing, or freezing the relevant property of the party concerned. For judgments and rulings that have become legally effective, the people's court may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), notify the units that have the obligation to assist in enforcement to provide such assistance in accordance with the law.

2. Where, during the trial of an economic dispute case, a people's court discovers illegal acts such as buying and selling on margin or short, subcontracting for profit, illegal transfer, bribery, or other illegal acts that harm the interests of the state and the public interest but do not yet constitute a crime, it shall handle the matter in accordance with the provisions of the Notice of the State Council Guo Fa [1982] No. 73 issued on May 4, 1982, namely: "Generally, there is no need to refer the matter to the administrative department for industry and commerce for handling; instead, the court may handle it in accordance with the law. This can simplify the work procedures and facilitate the timely handling of the case. In certain special circumstances where it is inconvenient for the court to handle the matter directly (e.g., the defendant is located elsewhere, etc.), the matter may be transferred to the relevant administrative department for industry and commerce for handling."

3. Where, during the trial of an economic dispute case, a people's court discovers economic crimes, especially serious economic crimes, criminal liability must be pursued; it must not simply treat the case as an economic dispute and let the criminals off. The people's court shall, in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the Criminal Procedure Law, promptly transfer the relevant clues and materials concerning the crime to the public security organs or the people's procuratorates for investigation and handling. In this regard, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security jointly issued Notice Fa (Yan) Fa [1985] No. 17 on August 19, 1985, which all levels of people's courts must strictly implement.

4. With respect to criminal offenders discovered in economic dispute cases, in order to prevent them from escaping, colluding in confessions, or engaging in other acts harmful to society, the people's court may, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 38, 39, and 40 of the Criminal Procedure Law and based on the specific circumstances of the case, take measures such as summoning by force, obtaining a guarantor pending trial, or residential surveillance, or decide on arrest. Residential surveillance and arrest shall be executed by the public security organs in accordance with the law.

5. Where, during the trial of an economic dispute case, a people's court encounters conduct that obstructs litigation, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 77 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), take necessary coercive measures depending on the gravity of the circumstances, up to and including pursuing criminal liability in accordance with the law; any person who, by means of violence or threats, refuses to execute a judgment or ruling of a people's court that has become legally effective shall be pursued for criminal liability in accordance with the provisions of Article 157 of the Criminal Law.

6. Recently, it has been discovered that, with respect to some serious economic crimes, the relevant departments have only imposed administrative penalties such as confiscation or fines, and have not transferred the cases to the judicial authorities for the pursuit of criminal liability in accordance with the law. This is highly unfavorable to ensuring the smooth implementation of the reform of the socialist economic system and the policies of opening up to the outside world and invigorating the domestic economy. Where a people's court discovers such serious economic crime cases that have been leniently dealt with, it shall recommend that the competent department transfer the case to the judicial authorities for investigation and handling in accordance with the law, and shall inform the people's procuratorate or public security organ of the relevant circumstances, and at the same time, report to the superior people's court.

With respect to the above points, if any new circumstances or issues arise during implementation, please promptly report them to this Court.

December 9, 1985
